change_summary: Promoted the narrow Technology trend target-width override into `risk_engine.enrich_signals()` using single-source constant `TREND_TECH_TARGET_ATR_MULT = 6.0`, added a unit test proving only Technology trend signals are retargeted, and fixed one LLM attribution test assertion to match the current 0/N replay-off coverage denominator. Production backtests reproduced the runtime 6.0 ATR metrics across the fixed late_strong, mid_weak, and old_thin snapshot windows.

delta_metrics.gate4_basis: Accepted because EV improved in all three non-overlapping windows, late_strong Sharpe improved by 0.10, old_thin Sharpe improved by 0.17, and no tested window worsened drawdown or trade count.

hypothesis: The deferred-positive Technology trend exit-width result from exp-20260425-027 is a real production-path alpha, not a monkeypatch artifact. Promoting only `trend_long | Technology` to a 6.0 ATR target should preserve the fixed-window EV improvements while leaving entries, sizing, ranking, LLM, C strategy, and all non-Technology exits unchanged.

llm_metrics.blocker_relation: LLM soft ranking remains blocked by candidate-level replay coverage, so this alpha_search deliberately used a deterministic exit-width mechanism instead of LLM ranking.

next_retry_requires: Do not broaden this into all trend_long target widening; broad and entry-conditioned trend target widening were already rejected
Do not continue sweeping 6-8 ATR by default; 6.0 was selected because it improved all windows cleanly without reducing late_strong return
Future exit-alpha work needs a fresh winner-truncation audit outside Technology trend
notes: This iteration changed one independent causal variable: Technology trend target width. It did not treat LLM as the problem; it bypassed LLM soft ranking because replay coverage remains insufficient. The main risk is that wider Technology trend targets could give back gains in sharp reversals, but the fixed-window drawdown metrics did not worsen.
